Welcome to Oak Lodge School
Oak Lodge School is a special academy managed by Barnet Special Education Trust. It is funded to offer 195 places for students aged 11-19 with a wide range of learning difficulties.

I hope you find the information that you are looking for on this site. If you wish to visit our school in person, please make an appointment at any time. We welcome visitors throughout the year.

Welcome to Oak Lodge
Oak Lodge School is a special academy managed by Barnet Special Education Trust.
For the academy year 2025-26, we are funded for 195 places for students aged 11-19 with a wide range of learning difficulties.
The quality of our Autism practice has been awarded Advanced Status by the Autism Accreditation Award Committee of the National Autistic Society and we have also been judged ‘Outstanding’ in three successive OFSTED inspections, both as a maintained school and as an academy. A copy of the latest inspection report is available here. You may also link to our DfE Performance Tables Information.
The school site is highly accessible and able to include young people with physical disabilities in all its learning. We work hard to ensure that all members of the school feel safe and acquire high levels of self-esteem. Students can expect to follow a curriculum relevant to their needs, with increased opportunities for the development of social skills. Staff are totally committed to providing the best possible education for all; assessing each individual’s level of development and enabling them to make progress at their own pace to fulfil their unique potential. Parent Partnership
We welcome the involvement of parents and carers in supporting learning and personal development Many of our students find it hard to discuss their daily activities, feelings and wishes with others. So that we can understand our students better, interpret different behaviours and responses and engage them in meaningful dialogue, it is helpful that everyone involved between home and school is kept informed of significant events or changes of circumstance.
We encourage frequent contact to help parents, carers and staff ensure consistency in response to certain events or behaviours. This helps to make life seem more predictable and safe for many students and supports them to learn well and make good progress. The Barnet Council's Local Offer is also available to support families and schools.
In addition to Parental Consultation Evenings and the more formal Annual Review meeting, contact may take the form of a home/school book, regular informal telephone conversations or regular email. Parents are of course welcome to come into the school, by appointment, at any time.
There are often other opportunities for parents to be involved in the life of the school: at coffee mornings, workshops or other special events. Please check Parent Notices on our website, or see our newsletters for the latest information.

There are well-established links between the school, local further education colleges and training providers.
A careers adviser with a specialism in learning disabilities provides guidance for students from Year 8 onwards and supports their transition into further education, training or employment according to their individual circumstances.

MOON Partnership
As part of an ongoing strategy of school led self-improvement, Oak Lodge works in partnership with other special schools and academies in Barnet.
Within the partnership, schools work together to support each other and share best practice.
Collectively we are known as the MOON Partnership. The four original schools of the partnership have now welcomed Kisharon, Oak Hill and The Windmill Schools to this growing network of mutual support.

pageCache.pageTitle: Oak Lodge School - Care and Wellbeing
pageCache.text:
Care and Wellbeing
The welfare of your son or daughter is important to everyone at Oak Lodge. Our circle of support will ensure that your child receives the care needed to develop to the best of his or her ability.
Our classroom teams aim to provide an environment where each student is able to feel safe and cared for. However, we understand that there may always be a time where a young person may need further support to thrive successfully in school. We have a well-developed and multi-disciplinary pastoral team, coordinated by deputy headteachers, who are all here to help when needed.
If at any point you feel that extra support may be needed and there are issues that you wish to discuss with any member of staff please email or telephone the school to make an appointment.

Safeguarding
The students of Oak Lodge belong to a group of people who are, potentially, some of the most vulnerable to abuse in all its forms, for a number of reasons. Child protection is an integrated part of the ethos and practices of our school. We are a school where ‘Every Child Matters’. Promoting the social, physical, mental and emotional wellbeing of each student is at the heart of all of our practices. Children and young people have a fundamental right to be protected from harm. Our students have the right to expect us to provide them with a safe and secure environment.
